images.scene: Inside an old Brazilian corner fruit shop (quitanda). A single hand of about eight bananas hangs from a rusty iron hook by a piece of twine, large and close, occupying the LOWER HALF of the frame, in front of a bare dark plaster wall in deep shadow. Every banana is smooth, firm and unblemished, except ONE in the middle of the hand, which is visibly further along: skin heavily freckled with dark ripening spots, slightly softer, clearly different from its neighbours. Hard side light from a window rakes across the bunch, strong texture on the peels. Camera a little below the bunch, looking slightly up. The twine rises and dissolves into the pale haze above. No people, no faces, no text.

Camera resting on the worn wooden counter of an old Brazilian street-market fruit stall, looking along the counter at table level. In the foreground, very close and large, a hand of about eight bananas lies on the wood, filling the lower part of the frame; all the bananas are smooth and unblemished except ONE in the centre, heavily freckled with dark ripening spots, clearly more matured than the others. Further along the counter, more bunches and wooden crates recede and dissolve into the pale morning haze. Hard side light, strong texture on the peels and the wood grain. No people, no faces, no text.
